newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bosnia PM says reconstruction not fast enough.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia PM says reconstruction not fast enough.

text.p: Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic complained on Friday that his country was not being rebuilt quickly enough because some international donors were not meeting their pledges for reconstruction aid.

"The reconstruction so far has had disappointing results when rehabilitation of industry and creation of jobs are concerned," Muratovic told a meeting of central and eastern European leaders in Austria.

"The most sensitive problem of the reconstruction programme is that a number of pledges from donor conferences held in Brussels have not been fulfilled, and every excuse is used by certain donors to justify delays in implementation of their donations," he added, according to a text of his speech.
An international donor conference in April in Brussels pledged $1.8 billion for Bosnia's post-war reconstruction, of which $550 million has been dispersed so far.

"Charity is not sufficient to ensure stability and economic recovery. Bosnia now needs real international solidarity and partnership which would enable it to take its place in the world economy," Muratovic said.

He was speeking at a two-day meeting of the Central European Initiative, formed in 1989 to foster regional cooperation. Bosnia is scheduled to take over the presidency of the group, which is currently chaired by Austria, next year.
